title: Grand Theft Auto
notes: North American publishers: ASC Games (PC) and Take-Two Interactive (PlayStation); Game Boy Color published by Rockstar Games (infobox).

release.note: Wikipedia: EU: 28 November 1997; NA: 24 March 1998 … Grand Theft Auto, the first game in the series, was released for MS-DOS and Windows in November 1997, ported to the PlayStation in 1998 and the Game Boy Color in 1999.

title: Grand Theft Auto: London 1969
notes: Full name: Grand Theft Auto Mission Pack #1: London 1969.

in_universe.note: The expansion adheres to the same gameplay mechanics as the main game and takes place in a fictionalised version of London during the 1960s. … Category:Video games set in 1969

release.note: Wikipedia: released = 30 April 1999 … It was released for PC (MS-DOS and Windows) and PlayStation in April 1999.

links.note: expansion pack (Mission Pack #1) for Grand Theft Auto

title: Grand Theft Auto: London 1961
notes: Full name: Grand Theft Auto Mission Pack #2: London 1961; freeware PC download. No own article; the title redirects to the London 1969 article.

in_universe.note: It is much shorter in length, and features the same map and characters as London 1969, but takes place eight years prior. … Category:Video games set in 1961

release.note: Wikipedia: It was released on 1 July 1999 in tandem with and through the website for Grand Theft Auto 2.

links.note: prequel set eight years before London 1969

title: Grand Theft Auto 2
notes: Dreamcast 1 May 2000 (NA); Game Boy Color December 2000 (article prose).

in_universe.label: unspecified (c. 1999)
in_universe.note: The time period the game is set in is not specified—conflicting sources suggest anything from "three weeks into the future", to the year being 2013, despite in-game references to the "new millennium" that is coming (implying the game takes place around its time of release, in 1999).

release.note: Wikipedia: Grand Theft Auto 2 was released for the PlayStation and Windows on 22 October 1999.

title: Grand Theft Auto III
notes: Remastered in Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy – The Definitive Edition (11 November 2021).

in_universe.note: A redesigned version of Liberty City was introduced in Grand Theft Auto III (set in 2001).

release.note: Wikipedia: NA: 23 October 2001; PAL: 26 October 2001 … Grand Theft Auto III was released in October 2001 for the PlayStation 2, in May 2002 for Windows, and in November 2003 for the Xbox.

links.note: numbered sequel; starts a new (3D) continuity

in_universe.note: The game is set in 1986 in fictional Vice City, which is based heavily on the city of Miami, Florida.

release.note: Wikipedia: NA: 29 October 2002; EU: 8 November 2002 … The game was released in October 2002 for the PlayStation 2.

in_universe.note: In 1992, after five years in Liberty City, gangster Carl "CJ" Johnson (Young Maylay) returns to Los Santos following his mother's death in a drive-by shooting.

release.note: Wikipedia: NA: 26 October 2004; PAL: 29 October 2004 … The game was released for the PlayStation 2 in October 2004.

title: Grand Theft Auto Advance
notes: Top-down like the 2D games, but the article says "it is part of the series' "3D universe" canon".

in_universe.note: The game is set in 2000 within Liberty City, the same setting used for Grand Theft Auto III.

release.note: Wikipedia: vgrelease|NA|26 October 2004 … The eighth entry in the Grand Theft Auto series, it was released for the Game Boy Advance in October 2004.

links.note: prequel set one year before Grand Theft Auto III

title: Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories

external_ids.enwiki: Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories

in_universe.note: Liberty City Stories takes place in early 1998 within the fictional Liberty City (based on the real life New York City), and forms part of the "3D Universe" canon of the Grand Theft Auto series.

release.note: Wikipedia: 25 October 2005 … The ninth installment in the Grand Theft Auto series, it was initially released as a PlayStation Portable exclusive in October 2005.

links.note: prequel set three years before Grand Theft Auto III

title: Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories

external_ids.enwiki: Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories

in_universe.note: Vice City Stories takes place in 1984 within Vice City, and forms part of the "3D Universe" canon of the Grand Theft Auto series.

release.note: Wikipedia: NA: 31 October 2006; EU: 3 November 2006; AUS: 10 November 2006

links.note: prequel set two years before Vice City

in_universe.note: A third version of Liberty City was featured in Grand Theft Auto IV, its expansion packs The Lost and Damned and The Ballad of Gay Tony (all three set in 2008), and the handheld game Grand Theft Auto: Chinatown Wars (set in 2009).

release.note: Wikipedia: WW: 29 April 2008 … Grand Theft Auto IV was released for the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 consoles in April 2008, and for Windows in December.

links.note: numbered sequel; starts a new (HD) continuity

title: Grand Theft Auto IV: The Lost and Damned

external_ids.enwiki: Grand Theft Auto IV: The Lost and Damned

notes: PS3/Windows 13 April 2010 (NA) in the compilation Grand Theft Auto: Episodes from Liberty City, which has no own article (redirects to the franchise page).

in_universe.note: In 2008, Billy Grey (Lou Sumrall), president of the Lost Outlaw Motorcycle Club's Alderney chapter, is welcomed back by his fellow members after a period in a court-ordered rehabilitation facility.

release.note: Wikipedia: It was released individually for the Xbox 360 on 17 February 2009.

links.note: episodic expansion; story runs alongside GTA IV

title: Grand Theft Auto: The Ballad of Gay Tony

external_ids.enwiki: Grand Theft Auto: The Ballad of Gay Tony

notes: PS3/Windows 13 April 2010 (NA) via Episodes from Liberty City. Article revision is from 2023 (stable page).

in_universe.note: In 2008, shortly after witnessing the robbery of the Bank of Liberty, Luis Fernando Lopez (Mario D'Leon) meets with his boss and business partner, nightclub owner Anthony "Gay Tony" Prince (David Kenner).

release.note: Wikipedia: It was first released for the Xbox 360 on 29 October 2009 as a downloadable add-on for owners of Grand Theft Auto IV

links.note: episodic expansion; story runs alongside GTA IV

in_universe.note: In 2009, Triad member Huang Lee travels to Liberty City to deliver the Yu Jian sword

release.note: Wikipedia: 17 March 2009 … The game was released for the Nintendo DS in March 2009, PlayStation Portable in October 2009, iOS in January 2010, and Android and Fire OS devices in December 2014.

links.note: same Liberty City; the franchise article says the two games "are otherwise unrelated"

in_universe.label: 2013 (prologue 2004)
in_universe.note: A third version of San Andreas appeared in Grand Theft Auto V (set in 2013), again imagined as a state. … In 2004, criminals Michael Townley (Ned Luke), Trevor Philips (Steven Ogg), and Brad Snider (Ryan Woodle) partake in a failed robbery in Ludendorff, North Yankton, resulting in Michael being presumed dead.

release.note: Wikipedia: Grand Theft Auto V was released in September 2013 for the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360, in November 2014 for the PlayStation 4 and Xbox One, in April 2015 for Windows, and in March 2022 for the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. … 17 September 2013

title: Grand Theft Auto Online
notes: Ongoing live-service game. A standalone version was released 15 March 2022 for PS5/Xbox Series X/S. You might split it by major update later; one unit for now.

in_universe.label: 2013 onward
in_universe.note: The game's narrative begins in 2013, several months before Grand Theft Auto V. … In 2026, the player is recruited by Faber and Raf for a robbery of the Kortz Center's art gallery

release.note: Wikipedia: It was released on 1 October 2013 for the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360, 18 November 2014 for the PlayStation 4 and Xbox One, 14 April 2015 for Windows, and 15 March 2022 for the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

links.note: GTA V's online component; its story starts months before V

title: Grand Theft Auto VI
notes: Article: "no Windows release scheduled". Continuity gta-hd is inferred: the franchise article defines the HD universe as "Grand Theft Auto IV, its expansions and its sequels" and does not name VI explicitly.

in_universe.label: present day (2020s)
in_universe.note: A third version of Vice City was featured as a main setting in Grand Theft Auto VI (set in the present) and was again based on Miami. … It parodies 2020s American culture, with satirical depictions of social media and influencer culture

release.note: Wikipedia: After two delays, further leaks, and an extensive marketing campaign, it was released on 19 November 2026 for the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.
